Question: Let \(\Gamma\) be an arbitrary set, and let \(\ell_1(\Gamma)\) denote the Banach lattice of all scalar families \(x=(x_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) such that \(\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}|x_\gamma|<\infty\), equipped with its usual \(\ell_1\)-norm and pointwise order. Which statement gives the exact general validity of the semiprojectivity and \(1^+\)-projectivity properties for \(\ell_1(\Gamma)\) as \(\Gamma\) varies over all sets?
Predicted label: 'E'
Predicted text: 'For every set \\(\\Gamma\\), the Banach lattice \\(\\ell_1(\\Gamma)\\) is semiprojective, and in fact it is \\(1^+\\)-projective for every \\(\\Gamma\\), because every lattice homomorphism from \\(\\ell_1(\\Gamma)\\) into a separable Banach lattice is nonzero on at most countably many coordinate vectors.'
Correct label: 'C'
Correct text: 'For every set \\(\\Gamma\\), the Banach lattice \\(\\ell_1(\\Gamma)\\) is semiprojective, and it is \\(1^+\\)-projective if and only if \\(\\Gamma\\) is countable.'
Exact Match: 0.0
